title.narrative: Uganda: Community Justice Programme (CJP) in Uganda, 2018-2023

description.narrative: 1) To empower grassroot communities to claim and uphold their rights. 2) To strengthen the capacities of and linkages between formal and informal justice systems supporting effective redress mechanisms. 3) To strengthen the capacities to seek and deliver justice services for women and girls at the community level. 4) To develop a comprehensive oversight and monitoring framework to measure the functionality and impact of justice services delivered at the community level.
The project aims to enhance the accessibility, quality and sustainability of justice services delivered for rural, vulnerable and marginalized communities in Uganda.

Vulnerable and marginalized communities living in rural areas in Uganda, especially women, children, persons with disabilities, persons living with HIV, victims of conflict-related sexual and gender-based crimes, civil society organisations (CSO), academia, legal aid service provider networks, community legal volunteers and paralegals from non-state legal aid service providers, traditional and informal justice systems such as customary and clan social structures, religious authorities, and community-based court models.
